tasks.title: Careers afternoon priorities
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.subject: Careers afternoon – your ideas
paragraphs: As you know, our school is planning a careers afternoon for students next term. We want to help them think about future skills they will need. I need your help to decide on a few things.

First, should we focus on digital skills like coding and online safety, or on communication skills like speaking in public and working in a team? Which do you think is more important for students' future careers?
Also, we need to choose one practical activity for the afternoon. Would you prefer a workshop where students try a simple coding task, or a role-play activity where they practise a job interview?
Finally, can you suggest one way to make sure students remember what they learn after the event?

promptBlocks.heading: Notes for your reply
listItems: Say which focus you prefer (digital skills or communication skills) and explain why.
Choose an activity (coding workshop or interview role-play) and give a reason.
Suggest one way to help students remember what they learn.
Ask Mrs Hill about the date of the careers afternoon.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Mrs Hill using all the notes.

tasks.title: Future skills article
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: Our school magazine wants to hear your ideas about the careers afternoon.
What future skill do you think is most important for students to learn?
How can the careers afternoon help students prepare for jobs?
Write an article answering these questions and we will put it in the next magazine!

tasks.title: Careers afternoon story
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
"When the programme coordinator asked for a volunteer to try the virtual reality headset, nobody moved."
